turn.user_message: No, you are not getting it. I don’t need a questionnaire. I need to know why our beds sit empty for hours.
turn.note_for_review: Miss 2 in a row (not understood, high). The app shows the reset line. Tojo rechecks, then answers what was asked: why beds earn nothing for hours. One question only, with Something else.

text: Then let’s start with the why. In most hospitals your size, the bed stops earning long before it is empty, for four usual reasons.
They feed each other. One of them is usually a rule nobody wrote down: a bed is given only once it is ready. So nobody is called in until late, and the late arrival seems to prove the rule.
Which of the four sounds most like your hospital?

blocks.eyebrow: Why a bed earns nothing for hours
blocks.title: Four reasons, one loop
blocks.deck: The usual reasons in hospitals your size. Not yet checked against yours.

blocks.label: What usually keeps a bed from earning

items.title: Bed given only once ready
items.text: Nobody can be called in against a bed until it is nearly free. So arrivals drift to the afternoon.
more_points: The bed is put against a name only after the ward says it is ready.
So the next patient is called late.
The late arrival then seems to prove beds were never free earlier.

items.title: One team for both jobs
items.text: The same team does discharges in the morning and admissions after. The job with a deadline wins.
more_points: Discharges take the morning, until about noon to 2 PM.
Admissions are then booked for later in the day.
Two jobs that should overlap run one after the other.

items.title: Bill closed, patient still in bed
items.text: Billing stops when the final bill closes, late morning. The patient often stays until evening.
more_points: Insurance approval, payment and the family briefing all happen with the patient in the bed.
Nothing is charged to that bed all this time.

items.title: Cleaning told late
items.text: Housekeeping hears only once the patient has left, and may be short at the busy hour.
more_points: The clock for cleaning starts when someone tells housekeeping, not when the patient leaves.
Nobody has usually worked out how many beds they can ready at the busiest hour.

blocks.label: Dead bed time
blocks.value: Last bill closed to next bill opened
blocks.sub: Often half a day or more on one bed. Most hospitals have never measured it on its own.
